children: Accounts, payment railroad, app to Help Our Bureau Mumbai: State Bank of India expects to recover its costs and generate a surplus from the merchant discount rate (MDR) on eligible UPI transactions from October 15, a senior official at the country's largest bank said.

SBI will get a share of the MDR on each person-to-merchant (P2M) unified payment interface (UPI) transaction of more than 2,000 involving its accounts, the official said on the condition of anonymity. "Then we also have a payments railroad on the UPI network, which is not as famous as Google Pay or PhonePe but is still formidable," the official said. "We also have an application which has many customers on board. All this means that we will make a surplus." From October 15, P2M UPI payments above 2,000 will attract an MDR of 0.4%. This is the first time MDR is being charged on the hugely successful UPI payments since 2020. The charges would be split between the issuing bank, acquiring bank, payment gateways and UPI applications.

The issuing bank, or the payer's bank, is likely to receive 40% of the MDR, while the acquiring bank, or merchant's bank, will receive 30%. The payment gateway is set to get 20% and the application service 10%. "Since we are both a large acquiring and issuing bank, we will automatically get a large chunk of the amount," the SBI official said. "We also have a payment system and an application service, so it is fair to assume that we will make some money, though we have not done the calculations." He said SBI is still evaluating the MDR implications. "There are also reports that people will split the transactions to avoid charges, which means our volumes will increase but our value will not increase, and it will create pressure on our systems.

So we have to evaluate all those aspects," the official said. Replying to another question, the official said SBI has garnered $10 billion from FCNR (B) inflows which it is confident of deploying. "We annually garner 5.5 lakh crore from normal deposits, which we comfortably deploy; so another 90,000 crore should not be a problem," he said. "It could be a problem for smaller banks because it will mean they may have to enter new segments like corporate lending, but we will be able to manage."

title: MDR to Help Bring in a Surplus on UPI Deals: SBI Official
